project_overview.what: A frontend-only, fixture-driven prototype of DealForge V2 — static HTML, no backend, no infra.
project_overview.why: Lloyd needs to see and judge V2 changes before they are built, and Geri needs a precise target to build against in production DealForge rather than a written spec.
project_overview.end_state: Every V2 change is visible and clickable in the prototype, each documented in docs/changes/, with fixtures that define the API contract — handed to Geri to build for real.
project_overview.current_summary: Repo born standalone and scaffolded 2026-09-04. V1 frontend forked in from accounting-qs/dealforge @720ec7e. Source meeting analysed and recorded in reference/. Chat interface explicitly scoped OUT. Next: make the forked portal run without a server (fetch shim + fixtures), then build the case-study comparison across four tabs.

current_phase: Phase 1 - Reproduce V1 as a static prototype
current_focus: Get app/portal.html rendering from fixtures with no backend
immediate_next_steps: Build the fetch shim and a first job fixture so the portal renders standalone
Verify every tab paints from fixture data
Decide with Lloyd: real client case studies vs placeholders (gates the hosting decision)
Then Phase 2 — case-study comparison on lead-list, calendar-invite, webinar-experience, roi-model
resume_here: Repo scaffolded, V1 frontend forked in, source meeting recorded. Next task is the fetch shim + first job fixture so app/portal.html renders with no server.

tech_stack.hosting: local static server; GitHub Pages under consideration (blocked on the real-client-data question)

deploy_flow: none yet — static files, no infra
hard_constraints: Never call production DealForge, Supabase, Apollo, Anthropic, Fireflies or GHL. No credentials in this repo, ever.
Fork V1 markup rather than rewriting, so the handoff reads as a diff.
Every UI change gets an entry in docs/changes/ or it will not get built.
No real client data in fixtures without Lloyd's explicit approval.

recent_milestones.milestone: Standalone repo scaffolded, V1 frontend forked in from accounting-qs/dealforge @720ec7e
Source meeting (2026-09-04 sales training) analysed; requests recorded per tab in reference/

decision_log.decision: Born standalone — own repo from commit #1, not a branch of production DealForge
decision_log.reasoning: The prototype must never be confused with or able to affect the live app
Alex asked for it hard, but it is a separate product; folding it into DealForge turns every tab into a chat surface and nothing ships. V2 is UI-level changes plus the case-study library.

decision_log.decision: Fixture-driven with no backend, rather than a half-working app on a real database
decision_log.reasoning: The fixture files become the API contract Geri builds to — a working screen plus its exact data shape is more useful to a backend engineer than a written spec

decision_log.decision: Case-study comparison uses one shared control with two display modes — swap on lead-list/calendar-invite/webinar-experience, side-by-side on roi-model
decision_log.reasoning: One component and one data shape reused four times instead of four bespoke features; ROI needs both sets of numbers visible at once for the comparison to land

decision_log.decision: Repo lives under lloyd-yip, not accounting-qs
decision_log.reasoning: accounting-qs is a separate personal GitHub account, not an org — one user account cannot create repos under another. Geri has access to lloyd-yip, so no transfer is needed.
